cloudUsage.scope: 84 scored text cases only; excludes warm-ups, access probes, and audio trials

manualReview.finding: Frequently copied the testing-plan example from instructions, including a quote absent from the actual transcript. Existing grounding rejected it, which also explains many silent passes.
Named Maya or Alex as a follow-up owner without an assignment in the transcript, despite passing the automated topic-word checks.
Summary said venue cost was agreed upon; the transcript only states a price.
Suggested using the agenda item to choose a launch date; this passed the keyword check but did not give a useful method for choosing between dates.
Summary overstated a date merely considered as a date previously set; automated section checks did not catch this.

Key decisions, assignments and date distinctions were correct. Some supporting quotes cover only part of a note that combines facts across rows; passing this suite does not establish strict single-quote entailment.
Added a gendered pronoun not specified by the fixture; no owner or deadline was changed.

limitations: Checks include existing rules, grounding and controller behavior; they are not raw model accuracy or a real-meeting reliability score.
Some silent cases pass because unsupported model output is rejected by grounding. Apple baseline repeatedly copied a prompt example that was not in the transcript.
Apple compact prompts were written after baseline inspection; their scores are exploratory, not held-out.
Cloud timing is from this Mac/network on the standard service tier, not a universal cloud speed or SLA. No cloud model tournament was run.
Different tokenizers, native schema generation and cache behavior; equal output caps do not imply equal output lengths.
Apple system-model version follows macOS; the API did not provide a reproducible weight hash.
Audio trials use one easy prerecorded question repeated three times. No physical microphone, speaker routing, or real meeting was tested.
Apple requests use SystemLanguageModel.default on-device. Node/browser HTTP interception does not inspect Apple system-service traffic.
Cold launches, lengthy meetings, background contention and sustained battery/thermal behavior are not characterized.
